name: AI Compliance, Law and Regulation
blurb: State AI legislation and federal rulemaking, the frameworks, standards and enforcement records organisations are measured against - ISO 42001, the NIST AI RMF, the EU AI Act, SOC 2, the sector rules and the agencies actually bringing cases - and the separate body of siting, zoning and utility law that decides where AI compute may physically be built and who pays for the power it draws.

built.name: AI Laws by State
built.detail: Every tracked AI bill in all fifty states, DC, Puerto Rico, and Congress, one page per jurisdiction, refreshed daily from LegiScan.

built.name: AI Governance Frameworks
built.detail: ISO 42001, the NIST AI RMF, the EU AI Act, SOC 2, the sector rules, and the agency enforcement records, explained in plain English.

built.name: Federal AI Legislation
built.detail: Bills before Congress and federal rulemaking: 614 tracked congressional AI bills refreshed daily from LegiScan, 101 Federal Register documents from the rulemaking watch, the agency enforcement records (FTC, SEC, EEOC, CFPB, HHS OCR), and how existing federal statutes, HIPAA, FCRA, ECOA, COPPA, FERPA, GLBA, Title VII, the CFAA, apply to AI.

built.name: Global AI Laws
built.detail: The EU AI Act, the EU Cyber Resilience Act and product liability regime, GDPR as applied to AI, DORA, NIS2, China's AI regulations, and the Council of Europe Framework Convention, explained in plain English with the compliance obligations each creates.

built.name: Data Centre Siting, Power and Local Regulation
built.detail: Every other framework in this section governs what an AI system may do. This one governs where it may physically exist and what it may draw from the grid, and almost none of it mentions artificial intelligence. Five regimes decide it: state power siting boards, which in many states take exclusive jurisdiction above a megawatt threshold and leave a city able to ask but not require; municipal zoning, which can permit a campus of six million square feet and then prohibit any more, as Fayetteville, Georgia did in March 2026; public utility commissions, which rule on interconnection and on whether data centre load may be recovered from residential customers, as Georgia did when it froze base rates through 2028; environmental permitting, where an air permit may set no carbon limit at all because other pollutants fall below federal thresholds; and infrastructure thresholds, below which no approval is required, which is why an eight-inch gas pipeline serving one customer needs none. The page sets out each regime with the records behind it, the tax abatement terms three municipalities have published, and the four different power figures that siting documents use and directories routinely confuse.

built.name: Agency Enforcement Actions
built.detail: What federal agencies are actually bringing cases over, under powers they already have. An enforcement action is not a law: it is a regulator showing where an existing statute reaches AI today. The DOJ charging algorithmic price coordination under the Sherman Act, the FTC opening a personalised pricing docket, the SEC charging an AI founder with securities fraud. Each one is dated, linked to the agency's own announcement, and tracked as an event rather than a rule.

built.name: Enacted AI Laws
built.detail: Every AI-related bill that has actually become law, detected from the legislative record on the day its status changes, with the state, the date, and the source record for each.
